training_data: Pooled polysomnography cohort from the Sleep Medicine Laboratory of the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University and Guangdong Sanjiu Brain Hospital, Guangzhou (Mar-Dec 2024): 817 participants (478 non-aMCI/339 aMCI); training group 571 (random 70%); LASSO + multivariable logistic nomogram, training AUC 0.968
test_data: Validation group of 246 (random 30% of the same pooled two-hospital data); AUC 0.953
reason: The 'validation cohort' is a random 30% split of the same pooled two-hospital dataset, so both hospitals contributed to training and to testing; this is a held-out partition of the development data (V3), and the authors themselves say external validation is still needed.

quotes.quote: In this study, we collected data from middle-aged and elderly adults (aged ≥40 years) who underwent overnight PSG at the Sleep Medicine Laboratory of The Sixth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, and Guangdong Sanjiu Brain Hospital between March 2024 and December 2024.

The dataset was randomly divided into a training group (70 %) and a validation group (30 %) using the “sample” function in R. The training set was used to develop the predictive model, whereas the validation set was utilized to evaluate the performance and generalizability of the model.
The participants were then randomly split into training and validation groups at a 7:3 ratio, resulting in 571 individuals in the training group and 246 in the validation group

Third, this single-centre study was conducted in a relatively homogeneous population, which may limit the generalizability of our findings to other ethnic or regional groups. Hence, future studies involving multi-centre cohorts with more diverse populations are needed for the external validation of our nomogram.
